schoene:1903.author: Hermann Schöne (ed.)
schoene:1903.work: Heronis Alexandrini Opera quae supersunt omnia, Vol. III: Rationes dimetiendi et Commentatio dioptrica
schoene:1903.note: Editio princeps of Hero's Metrica (Books I–III) from Codex Constantinopolitanus Palatii Veteris 1, together with the critical Greek text of the Dioptra.

schmidt:1900.author: Wilhelm Schmidt & Ludwig Nix (eds.)
schmidt:1900.work: Heronis Alexandrini Opera quae supersunt omnia, Vol. II, Fasc. 1: Mechanica et Catoptrica
schmidt:1900.note: Critical edition of Hero's Catoptrica (William of Moerbeke's 1269 Latin text and Olympiodorus's verbatim Greek shortest-path fragment, pp. 368–372).

hultsch:1864.author: Friedrich Hultsch (ed.)
hultsch:1864.work: Heronis Alexandrini Geometricorum et Stereometricorum Reliquiae
hultsch:1864.note: Public-domain Greek critical edition of Hero's Definitiones and the Heronian metrological corpus.

heiberg:1912.author: Johan Ludvig Heiberg (ed.)
heiberg:1912.work: Heronis Alexandrini Opera quae supersunt omnia, Vol. IV: Heronis Definitiones cum variis collectionibus
heiberg:1912.note: Teubner standard section numbering of Hero's Definitiones collated with Hultsch (1864).

euclid:elements.author: Euclid
euclid:elements.locus: Books I–XIII (ed. Heiberg / trans. Heath, geometor/euclid & geometor/elements)
euclid:elements.note: Axiomatic foundation of Hero's synthetic proofs: Book II gnomons and obtuse/acute projections (II.12–13), Book III cyclic quadrilaterals (III.22), Book IV incircle (IV.4), Book VI similarity and areas (VI.4, VI.8, VI.19), Book XII exhaustion, and Book XIII golden-section regular polyhedra (XIII.8–18).

euclid:data.author: Euclid
euclid:data.note: Provides the deductive 'given' (δοθέν) analysis language used in every proposition of Hero's Metrica before the numerical synthesis (συντεθήσεται δὴ οὕτως).

euclid:divisions.author: Euclid
euclid:divisions.work: On Divisions of Figures (Περὶ διαιρέσεων βιβλίον)
euclid:divisions.locus: Preserved in Arabic epitome of al-Sijzī & Fibonacci's Practica geometriae
euclid:divisions.note: Classical precursor to Book III of Hero's Metrica on dividing plane figures into given area ratios; Hero generalizes the theory to arbitrary quadrilaterals, polygons, concentric circles, pyramids, cones, frusta, and spheres.

archimedes:circle.author: Archimedes
archimedes:circle.note: Cited explicitly in Metrica I.26 for Circle = (1/2) * circumference * radius and the rational bound π ≈ 22/7 (giving Circle : d² ≈ 11 : 14).

archimedes:sphere-cylinder.author: Archimedes
archimedes:sphere-cylinder.work: On the Sphere and Cylinder (Περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου)
archimedes:sphere-cylinder.locus: Books I–II (I.33–34, I.42–43, II.2; ed. Heiberg Vol. I)
archimedes:sphere-cylinder.note: Cited in Metrica I.37–39 (spherical surface = 4 great circles; spherical segment surface = circle of radius equal to polar chord) and Metrica II.11–12 & III.23 (sphere = 2/3 circumscribing cylinder; spherical segment volume; cutting a sphere in a given ratio).

archimedes:parabola.author: Archimedes
archimedes:parabola.note: Cited in Metrica I.32 & I.35 for the exact 4/3 ratio of any parabolic segment to the inscribed triangle of equal base and height, and used heuristically in I.31–33 to bound circular segments.

archimedes:conoids.author: Archimedes
archimedes:conoids.work: On Conoids and Spheroids (Περὶ κωνοειδέων καὶ σφαιροειδέων)
archimedes:conoids.note: Cited in Metrica I.34 for the exact area of an ellipse (πab, the circle whose diameter is the geometric mean √(2a·2b) of the axes).

archimedes:method.author: Archimedes
archimedes:method.work: The Method of Mechanical Theorems (Περὶ τῶν μηχανικῶν θεωρημάτων πρὸς Ἐρατοσθένην ἔφοδος / Ἐφοδικόν)
archimedes:method.note: Cited by name (ἐν τῷ Ἐφοδικῷ) in Metrica I.32, II.14, and II.15 for the cylindrical ungula (hoof = 1/6 circumscribing square prism) and the bicylinder groin vault (2/3 circumscribing cube). Hero's Metrica was the sole surviving witness to these theorems until Heiberg discovered the Archimedes Palimpsest in 1906.

archimedes:plinthides.author: Archimedes
archimedes:plinthides.work: On Plinths and Cylinders (Περὶ πλινθίδων καὶ κυλίνδρων — lost)
archimedes:plinthides.note: Lost Archimedean treatise cited solely by Hero in Metrica I.26 as containing finer rational bounds for the circumference-to-diameter ratio before simplifying to 22 : 7 for practical mensuration.

dionysodorus:speira.author: Dionysodorus
dionysodorus:speira.work: On the Torus (Περὶ τῆς σπείρας — lost)
dionysodorus:speira.note: Lost Hellenistic treatise whose central theorem—expressing the volume of a torus (σπεῖρα) as 2π²Rr²—survives exclusively through Hero's Metrica II.13.

apollonius:conics.author: Apollonius of Perga
apollonius:conics.note: Underpins Metrica I.34 (ellipse as oblique section of a right circular cylinder) and II.1–4 (oblique cones and cylinders).

proclus:in-euclidem.author: Proclus Diadochus
proclus:in-euclidem.work: Commentary on the First Book of Euclid's Elements
proclus:in-euclidem.note: Companion GEOMETOR treatise preserving five explicit testimonies to 'Heron the Mechanician' on postulate economy, direct proof without reductio, and alternative Euclidean constructions.

pappus:synagoge.author: Pappus of Alexandria
pappus:synagoge.note: Companion GEOMETOR treatise; generalizes Hero's Metrica II.13 'unrolled torus' argument to arbitrary solids of revolution and preserves fragments of Hero's Mechanics.

heath:1921.author: Sir Thomas Little Heath
heath:1921.work: A History of Greek Mathematics, Vol. II: From Aristarchus to Diophantus
heath:1921.locus: Oxford: Clarendon Press, Ch. XVIII ('Heron of Alexandria'), pp. 298–354
heath:1921.note: Classic public-domain English mathematical analysis of the chronology of Hero, the Constantinople manuscript of the Metrica, Prop. I.8, square- and cube-root iteration, Catoptrica, and Dioptra.

wildberger:2005.author: Norman J. Wildberger
wildberger:2005.work: Divine Proportions: Rational Trigonometry to Universal Geometry
wildberger:2005.locus: Wild Egg Books, Ch. 7 (Archimedes' Function & Quadrea, geometor/wildberger W.07)
wildberger:2005.note: Companion GEOMETOR formalization expressing 16Δ² purely polynomially in side quadrances Q₁, Q₂, Q₃ as A = (Q₁+Q₂+Q₃)² − 2(Q₁²+Q₂²+Q₃²).

kimberling:etc.author: Clark Kimberling
kimberling:etc.note: Companion GEOMETOR registry of triangle centers; X(1) (the incenter H of Hero's Metrica I.8 diagram) has trilinears 1 : 1 : 1 and barycentrics a : b : c.
